newsitem.title: INDIA: Ford arm to set up component plants in India.
newsitem.headline: Ford arm to set up component plants in India.

text.p: Ford Auto Components and Electrical Group, a division of Ford Motor Co, is setting up two component plants in India, a senior official of Mahindra Ford India Ltd said on Friday.
Mahindra Ford is a joint venture between India's Mahindra and Mahindra and Ford to manufacture 25,000 Ford Escorts and 60,000 Ford Fiestas annually.
Its plant is located on the outskirts of the southern city of Madras. It sold its first locally manufactured car in October 1996.

"The two component plants will be adjacent to our facilities in Madras, and will be heavily export oriented," Jim Johnston, vice president sales and marketing at Mahindra Ford, told a news conference.
He did not give any investment figures but said the component plants will supply several car manufacturers in India and overseas.

Johnston said Korea's Hyundai Motor Co had an agreement with Ford for components worldwide, and that it would supply Hyundai in India. Hyundai's India plant is also located on the outskirts of Madras.
On what components would be manufactured in India, Johnston said that wire harnesses, dashboards and other plastic and glass parts would constitute some of the production.
The components manufactured in India will help Mahindra Ford achieve its target of 50 percent local content in its Indian cars.

"We are currently at 35 percent local content in our Escorts. Our endeavour is to increase this to 50 percent by the end of this financial year," he said, referring to the 1997/98 year ending next March 31.
